svg.title: The same MGW synergy can accompany different added target information
svg.desc: Exact finite categorical population comparison in nats. A, B and U are mutually independent fair bits. Baseline A and target Y=(A,B) are shared. Candidate C is U in the first column and B in the second; each source pair is uniform on four pairs. The four signed MGW atoms are redundancy ln(4/3), unique A ln(3/2), unique C minus ln(4/3) for U and ln(3/2) for B, and synergy ln(4/3) in both columns. Unique C plus synergy equals I(C;Y given A), which is zero for U and ln 2 for B. The full decomposition therefore retains the distinction. Signed cancellation is already in the MGW RndErr example. Priority of this matched comparison is unestablished. Explanatory figure. The table states exact finite-law values; the picture itself is not a proof or deployment evidence.
svg.text: Finite categorical MGW shared exclusions · signed population atoms · nats
Shared law: A, B and U are mutually independent fair bits.
Baseline A; target Y = (A, B); added candidate C is U or B.
Both source pairs have P(A = a, C = c) = 1/4 for a, c in {0, 1}.

g.text: Unique added C + net synergy = added conditional MI
Synergy ties; the full signed decomposition retains the CMI difference.
Signed cancellation is published in MGW (RndErr, §VI.3 / Table III).
Matched comparison: priority unestablished; no estimator or deployment claim.
